subject: Post-call: ByteFlux integration — auth, routing, retries & idempotency
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Subject: Post-call: ByteFlux integration — auth, routing, retries & idempotency

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. Quick recap and recommended next steps from the integration/architecture side so your engineering team can evaluate risk and estimate effort: 

Summary of what we discussed:
- Scope: SDK onboarding + auth, request routing for multi-region failover, structured output/tool-calling for agent flows, embeddings + reranker for search relevance, and robust rate-limit/retry/idempotency behavior for ingestion and serving.
- Primary goals: predictable latency for live features, safe background ingestion with dedup semantics, and clear quotas for cost forecasting.

Immediate technical notes / recommendations:
1) Auth & keys
   - We support API keys (rotatable), OAuth client credentials, and VPC/mTLS for Private deployments. For ByteFlux I recommend API keys + quarterly rotation; we can layer KMS-backed key wrapping if you want server-side rotation.
   - SDKs: set up auth via the SDK's credential provider (see attached sdk_quickstart.zip). Short-lived tokens work better for browsers/services with delegated access.

2) Routing & model fallback
   - Route by region header (X-Redwood-Region) with automatic fallback to our secondary region. For cost-sensitive flows, route to lower-cost model variants (e.g., quantized v1-small) and only escalate to high-quality models on explicit flags.

3) Structured output & tool calling
   - Use the SDK's structured output mode for deterministic JSON responses + verification hook. For tool-calling, we recommend the function schema plus a validation layer on your side to avoid unsafe exec.

4) Embeddings vs. Reranker
   - Pattern: use embeddings for candidate selection (sparse->dense hybrid) and a lightweight reranker to reorder top-K for production. Reranker adds ~10–30ms depending on model choice; we can quantify with a quick perf run.

5) Rate limits, quotas, and retries (high level)
   - Tenant-level token bucket with route-specific buckets (interactive vs. batch). See attached rate_limit_matrix.xlsx for rough starting buckets.
   - 429s: use exponential backoff with full jitter. Recommended base: 250ms, cap: 30s, max_retries: 6 for idempotent calls.
   - 5xx: allow fewer retries (3) and increment alerting if >5% error rate per minute.

6) Idempotency & deduplication
   - Add an Idempotency-Key header (UUID) for client requests that mutate state or are expensive (batch ingest). Server maintains short dedup store (recommend 24h but configurable). For background ingestion prefer job-based async API with job_id and status endpoints so clients can poll instead of blind retries.

Attachments included:
- rate_limit_matrix.xlsx (starter quotas)
- sdk_quickstart.zip (sample auth config + quickstart)

Proposed next steps / owners:
- Redwood to share a short integration design doc (Dev) — due Thu 2026-07-01 (Dev Patel)
- ByteFlux to confirm preferred auth (API keys vs OAuth) and target RPS for interactive features — due Fri 2026-07-02 (Liam)
- Schedule focused follow-up (30–45m) to review rate-limit matrix and reranker latency tradeoffs — propose Tue 2026-07-06 10am PT

If this matches what you captured, I’ll have Dev put together the integration doc and a one-page operational runbook for early-stage quotas and idempotency rules.

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa — this is super helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our engineering lead: 

1) Long-running ingestion: we have a daily bulk feed that currently retries on any failure. What's the recommended pattern so we don't double-index when retries happen? Is Idempotency-Key per-document sufficient, or do you recommend batching with a job_id approach?

2) Reranker latency: for our search UI we need sub-150ms p95. Can the reranker with embedding candidates meet that without blowing cost? If not, should we do a hybrid (local cheap rerank + server-side final rerank)?

3) Quotas: procurement will want hard caps and contact points before we move to a contract. Can you send an initial suggestion we can hand to procurement?

Subject: Re: Post-call: ByteFlux integration — auth, routing, retries & idempotency

On Mon, Jun 29, 2026 at 4:05 PM Liam Carter <liam@byteflux.com> wrote:
> 1) Long-running ingestion: we have a daily bulk feed that currently retries on any failure. What's the recommended pattern so we don't double-index when retries happen? Is Idempotency-Key per-document sufficient, or do you recommend batching with a job_id approach?

Good questions — short answers and practical suggestions below.

Ingestion / dedup patterns:
- Best practice: use job-based async ingestion for large batches. Client uploads chunk(s) and receives a job_id. The job processing is server-side and idempotent by job_id; if the client retries the upload you get the same job_id and can query status.
- For streaming or per-document calls, include an Idempotency-Key per logical item. Idempotency-Key should be a stable hash of the document ID + source timestamp (or a UUID assigned by your ingestion pipeline).
- Server-side dedup store: keep processed idempotency keys for a window (24h default). We can tune per your retention/volume.

Retry/backoff specifics (recommended):
- 429 handling: exponential backoff with full jitter. Example: sleep = random(0, base * 2^attempt); base=250ms; cap=30s; max_attempts=6 for idempotent flows.
- Non-idempotent operations: avoid client-side automatic retries. Instead, require an explicit retry token flow or surface the failure to the caller.
- For batch jobs, return a 202 + job_id and an idempotency-safe polling endpoint (/jobs/{job_id}/status).

Reranker latency tradeoffs:
- Reranker-only on top-K (K=10–50) typically adds modest latency; if you need p95 <150ms we should benchmark with your corpus and candidate set size. Hybrid approach (local lightweight model for first-pass, server-side for heavy re-rank) is a good way to balance cost & latency.

Procurement-friendly quotas:
- We will provide a starter quota proposal (per-minute token limits for interactive routes, daily quotas for background ingestion, and overage/circuit-breaker thresholds). See attached rate_limit_matrix.xlsx. I’ll ask Solutions Engineering to convert that into a procurement-friendly table.

I’ve attached a short snippets file (retry_patterns_snippets.md) with example header usage and a tiny pseudo-code block you can paste into your client.

Sample headers (recommended):
Idempotency-Key: <uuid>
X-Redwood-Request-Id: <uuid>  # request tracing for support
Authorization: Bearer <token>

Example pseudo-flow for background import:
- Client: POST /imports with metadata, returns 202 + job_id
- Server: accept chunks (PUT /imports/{job_id}/chunks), process async, dedupe by Idempotency-Key inside job
- Client: poll /imports/{job_id}/status or subscribe to webhook on completion

Let us know if you want us to draft the integration YAML with recommended SDK settings — Dev can own the doc and we can iterate.

Best,
Marissa

Adding a few concrete SDK/config knobs that make implementation straightforward for ByteFlux engineers: 

SDK config suggestions (defaults we propose in the integration YAML):
- max_retries: 6  # for idempotent endpoints
- retry_backoff_base_ms: 250
- retry_backoff_cap_ms: 30000
- jitter: true
- idempotency_window_seconds: 86400  # 24h dedup window
- idempotency_enabled: true  # opt-in per route
- async_job_chunk_size: 500  # docs per chunk for your pipeline (tunable)
- sparse_candidate_cutoff: 200  # for embedding -> reranker pipeline

Operational implementation notes:
- Rate limiting: tenant-level token bucket implemented in Redis with per-route keys. Use a small leaky bucket for interactive routes to keep p95 tight and allow short bursts.
- Dedup store: Redis or DynamoDB for keys with TTL; for high-volume ingestion use Redis clustered with LFU eviction plus a write-ahead log to S3 for recovery.
- Observability: emit metrics for 429 rate, retry attempts, dedup hits/misses, and job durations. We’ll wire these into the Console dashboards and alerts.

I’ll draft the integration YAML and a minimal sequence diagram (upload -> job -> dedupe -> index) and drop them into the Drive link in 24 hours. If ByteFlux can confirm target RPS and typical batch sizes, I’ll size the dedup store and rate buckets.

Action items (owners & dates):
- Dev: integration YAML + sequence diagram -> 2026-07-01 (dev_patel)
- Marissa: procurement quota table for contract -> 2026-07-02 (marissa_cole)
- ByteFlux: confirm auth choice + target RPS + batch size -> 2026-07-02 (Liam)
- Joint: follow-up call to review quotas & perf -> propose 2026-07-06 10am PT

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if you want to walk through the YAML.
